title: Recognition of a reduced flat pullback by its ideal and closed support
statement: Let $i:T\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_T)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] and closed image $Z=i(T)$. Let $g:Y\to X$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and write $P=T\times_XY$ and $q:P\to Y$ for the pullback and its projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume that $P$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Then $q$ is a closed immersion with image $g^{-1}(Z)$, and the canonical map $g^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_Y$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sfb-tensor-pullback-structure-sheaf-map] is injective with image equal to the vanishing ideal $\mathcal I_{g^{-1}(Z)}$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. There is a unique isomorphism $e:P\xrightarrow{\sim}(g^{-1}(Z))_{\mathrm{red}}$ over $Y$, so that $i_{g^{-1}(Z)}\circ e=q$, where $i_{g^{-1}(Z)}$ is the reduced induced closed immersion. No reducedness of $T$ or Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion), 01JT (lemma-points-fibre-product), and 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), combined with the flat ideal formula of lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change; extracted from item proof step 1.

proof.text: Apply lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image to i and g. It gives the closed pullback immersion and its kernel ideal as the image of the pulled-back ideal inclusion followed by the adjoint structure map. Compare its adjunction with the one defining tensorPullbackObjUnitToUnit using leftAdjointUniq. Naturality makes the composites differ by precomposition with an isomorphism, so their image subobjects agree. The structure map is an isomorphism by lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf.

By lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective, tensor pullback along g preserves finite limits and hence monomorphisms. Thus the pulled-back ideal inclusion followed by the structure isomorphism is monic. Its image equality from step 1 gives an isomorphism to the kernel ideal module over Y, compatible with inclusion. Evaluating this isomorphism on any open and composing with the injective kernel ideal inclusion proves injectivity there.

Use Scheme.Pullback.range_snd, the whole-source specialization of lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image, to obtain range(q) = preimage(g, range(i)). The support_ker formula and closedness of the range of i identify this with the closed subset W = preimage(g, support(ker(i))). Apply the uniqueness clause of lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme to q, whose source is reduced by hypothesis. It gives ker(q) = vanishingIdeal(W) and the unique isomorphism over Y. Substitute that ideal equality into the image subobject identity of step 1.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-O1-2ac73d42f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full; it is sound and needs no changes. Scope: no new nodes. The item's statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are byte-identical to live, where the item is still unsplit with no repair note and no other group's split. The proof is a three-step assembly. Step 1: lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change (its general clause plus its flat clause, Stacks 01JU(1) with 02N4) shows q is a closed immersion and that g^*I->O_Y is injective with image equal to the ideal ker(O_Y->q_*O_P) of def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf. Step 2: lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image (a Mathlib leaf, 01JT) with C=T gives q(P)=g^{-1}(Z), which is closed because g is continuous. Step 3: clause (3) of lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme (01J3), applied to q, which is a closed immersion with reduced source P and image W, gives that the ideal of q equals I_W and that there is a unique e with i_W∘e=q. Every hypothesis is checked and the steps use only the statements of the cited nodes. The parent lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent step 1 uses exactly these conclusions. Edge cases checked: T empty; X=Spec k[ε]/ε² with g=id, where Y is not reduced; the non-flat closed immersion V(t)->A^1, which shows flatness is needed; g=id with T=V(t²), which shows reducedness of P is needed; no Noetherian hypothesis is used anywhere. Duplicate search with rg -L over the DAG for 'reduced induced' with 'flat' and for statements that a pullback is the reduced induced subscheme found no duplicate. I accept the declared tool_uses: lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change (sk-thm-picard-rr) and lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme (sk-thm-p1) are generic scheme tools. No coefficient category or six-functor base-change morphism is involved, and no SGA source is cited.
